newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada 1996/97 crop production estimates - official.
newsitem.headline: Canada 1996/97 crop production estimates - official.

text.p: Canadian farmers estimate they will produce the following amounts of crops in the 1996/97 crop year, ending next July 31, according to a poll done by Statistics Canada.
The Statistics Canada survey was conducted from October 23 to November 15. The agency did not provide comparison figures for the 1995/96 crop year.
Statistics Canada said the November crop production estimates were final for this crop year, but revisions to them could be made for up to two years after the end of the crop year.

The agency said total wheat production in 1996/97 was expected to be 201 million bushels higher than in the previous crop year, due to higher yields and a 14 percent rise in seeded acreage. The highest production on record is 1.18 billion bushels in 1990 and this year's production was expected to reach 1.12 billion bushels.

Barley production was expected to reach a record 731 million bushels in 1996/97. Statistics Canada said this was the result of an increase of 1.6 million seeded acres and record yields in Saskatchewan. The previous record was set in 1986 at 669 million bushels.
Canola production was estimated to drop 62 million bushels in 1996/97 from the previous crop year, due to a 4.4 million acre decline in seeded area.
